in_hebrew.name: שבסטינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שבסטינה (Sebastina) היא שם נשים המורכב משמות יווניים, שבסטין (Sebastinos), שפירושו 'העומד מאחור' או 'השקט'. השם Sebas- נגזר מהמילה 'שב' (seb) שפירושה 'אל' או 'בעל' ו-'אסטין' (estin) המשמעות 'העומד' או 'השקט'. שם נשים זה מופיע בקורת כמאה ותשעים שנה כשמן של שלושת קדושים, שבסטיאן, שבסטינה ושבסטיאנוס, שנרצחו על ידי סקלי.

in_greek.name: Σεβαστινή
in_greek.long_meaning: Σεβαστινή (Σεβαστινή) είναι ένα γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από τα ελληνικά. Η ρίζα του ονόματος είναι η λέξη 'Σεβαστινος' (Σεβαστινος), που σημαίνει 'ο σέβαστος' ή 'ο σεβασμένος'. Το όνομα Σεβαστινή σχετίζεται με την ιδέα της σοφίας, της ηρωικής καλλιέργειας και της εκτίμησης. Στη Βυζαντινή Αυτοκρατορία, το όνομα Σεβαστινή ήταν δημοφιλές και συνδέθηκε με την εκκλησιαστική ζωή.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Sebastiana is a female variant of Sebastian, meaning 'venerated, revered.' In Christian tradition, Saint Sebastian is symbolic of endurance and resistance in the face of persecution, making Sebastiana a name representing strength and unwavering faith.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Saint Sebastian was a third-century Roman soldier who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Diocletian. He is said to have refused to abandon the Christian faith and was therefore sentenced to death. He was tied to a tree and shot with arrows, but did not die immediately. He was discovered still alive a few days later, and was clubbed to death. Sebastian became a popular saint in the Christian tradition and was associated with healing and protection from plague. In the Middle Ages, he was often depicted in art as a young, naked man with arrows piercing his body. His feast day is celebrated on January 20. Sebastiana, a feminized form of Sebastian, was believed to offer the same protection and healing powers to women.

Another legend associates Saint Sebastian with the Roman Emperor Elagabalus (218-222 AD), who is said to have attempted to force the people of Rome to abandon their traditional gods and worship the Syrian sun god Elagabal. During this time, there was a great famine in Rome, and the people turned to Sebastian for help. According to legend, Sebastian interceded with God on their behalf, and the famine was ended. In gratitude, the people of Rome hailed him as a savior, and he was later martyred for his faith.
